results.title: Exact skyline likelihood; singular and common-support information
claims: On x-ordered k-point interior antichains the normalized density is (N)_k product_i f(z_i) mu(D(s))^(N-k), with no k! divisor. Conditional invisible routes are iid draws truncated to the dominated region, once visible labels are fixed.

For the hard pair, K=n+1 is the entire alternative singular component; its probability satisfies 0<p_n<1/(n+1)! by strict TP2. Waiting only for this support event has alternative mean > (n+1)! and never terminates under the baseline.

After conditioning the alternative on K<=n, both directions of KL against the baseline are finite and strictly positive for every fixed n. This separates ordinary likelihood information from singular support evidence.
Exact/stable dominated-strip formulas and exact n=1 masses are given. Numerical quadrature is not a certified error bound.
limits: No sharp skyline divergence asymptotics, optimal testing rate, finite exact recovery of arbitrary reals, distribution-free actual route count, or physical access conclusion.
Dominated routes remain invisible in an individual endpoint function. Factorial waiting applies only to support-only detection, not all skyline tests.
fresh_local_contribution: Written specialization, normalized ordered density and hidden law, stable strip representation, factorial rarity and finite strictly positive common-support KL.

results.title: Count mean gap, TP2 record coupling and improved vector upper bound
claims: E0 K=H_n and E1 K=H_n+delta_n, with delta_n=(H_n-1)/(n^2-1) for n>1 and delta_1=(zeta(2)-1)/2.

Conditional quantile coupling under TP2 gives K<=R_(n+1) pathwise. Subtracting the exact squared mean from the coupled second moment yields Var1 K<=V_(n+1)+H_(n+1)^2-(H_n+delta_n)^2=O(log n). Joe record indicators are not assumed independent.
The midpoint test on independent ideal retained vectors has each error <=4 max(V_n,W_n)/(s delta_n^2), giving O_alpha(n^4/log n) vectors for fixed error.

With matched error, reset, started-vector and unconditional termination assumptions, this improves vector cost over the inherited strongest face-only Omega_alpha(n^4) bound, including arbitrary adaptive face-only words.
limits: No optimal skyline rate or matching lower bound. No total endpoint-probe advantage follows from the ideal vector bound.
The mean gap alone is insufficient: the coupling and variance subtraction carry the rate. Exact ideal readout is not asserted to be a physical operation.
fresh_local_contribution: Written exact mean specialization, quantile-record domination, variance subtraction and count test comparison.
inherited_not_newly_discovered_or_reprov: Parent supplied expectation/TP2 candidates and independently the same coupling and sharper variance subtraction; shared derivation, not duplicate independent discovery credit.

results.title: Finite rational-grid extraction and error-budget transport
claims: Quantization Q_L(x)=ceil(Lx) preserves grid endpoint responses. The binary-search staircase extracts exactly all distinct quantized minima, including ties, duplicates, endpoints and empty input, in T<=K_L+1+2 K_L ceil(log2(L+1)) probes.
Pathwise K_L<=K; coordinate-bin injectivity suffices for equality. Under either hard-pair world, P(K_L!=K)<=m(m-1)L^(-c). Across R vectors the mismatch probability is at most Rm(m-1)L^(-c).

Choosing the ideal test budget R and least integer L with L^n q^(n+1)>=p^(n+1), p/q=m(m-1)R/eta, realizes per-world error <=alpha+eta. A fully rational n=1 repair uses R>=ceil(16/alpha) and threshold 1+1/8.

For fixed total error below one half, the finite protocol realizes O(n^4/log n) independent vectors and the inherited face-only comparison. Total probe bounds are O(n^5) worst case and O(n^4 log n) expected.
limits: These upper bounds do not establish improved total-probe complexity or optimality. Physical precision, computation, retention and resets are uncharged resources.

Requires known n/c/calibration, independently refreshed vectors, noiseless rational endpoint access and exact comparisons. No arbitrary-real exact reconstruction, unknown-calibration uniformity, noise or laboratory validation.

Within-vector thresholds are unchanged throughout separately read nonlatched queries; the endpoint is the OR over coordinate-separable threshold-AND routes.
Fresh vectors are independent for the statistical test; repeated commands on one vector do not create fresh samples.
